node.statement: F2 GAUSS-LEMMA FRAME — E1's exact identification (2026-07-10, campaign cycle 93): the parity field is a GENERALIZED GAUSS'S-LEMMA SYMBOL. (a) U_c = #{x in G : c.xbar(x) mod q > q/2} is exactly the Gauss-lemma count with the fundamental half-interval [1,(q-1)/2] replaced by the subgroup orbit configuration; Gauss's lemma itself ((-1)^U = Legendre(a) for the interval with linear map) verified with 0 mismatches at q = 97 — the classical case IS the interval case of our object. (b) K_c = (X_0 + a X_2)/q - sum_x floor((x + a x^2)/q) (X_i = integer representative sums) — an EXACT floor-sum lattice count under n lines of slopes x^2/q; identity verified exactly at 4 rows, all a. So eps_c = (-1)^{K+U} is a Gauss-lemma-type parity of a lattice-point configuration — the E1 lattice identification is COMPLETE and classical machinery is now correctly named: Gauss/Eisenstein lemmas, Zolotarev permutation signs, Duke-Hopkins group-theoretic reciprocity. (c) NEGATIVE (measured): the naive Zolotarev candidate — eps as the sign of the sorting permutation of the orbit values — is REFUTED (correlation 0.00-0.07 at 4 rows); and satellite 26 already shows eps is no character. THE STRUCTURAL READING: every classical proof of quadratic reciprocity exploits the fundamental-domain specialness of the half-interval (a group-quotient structure subgroup orbits do not have); its absence here is exactly CONSISTENT with the certified pseudorandomness of eps in all spectral bases. The summit is now nameable in one sentence: PROVE SQUARE-ROOT CANCELLATION FOR GENERALIZED GAUSS-LEMMA PARITIES OF SUBGROUP ORBIT CONFIGURATIONS — a precisely-anchored, genuinely open problem adjacent to (but outside) classical reciprocity. Verifier: inline in campaign log #105 (local, small). Twenty-seventh satellite; E1's identification phase closed — what remains of E1/E2 is the open reciprocity/cancellation step itself.
